1  COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  MFA No. 20060 of 2010  JUDGMENT Challenging impugned judgment and award dated 01.09.2008 passed by Additional Civil Judge (Sr.
Dn) and A.M.A.C.T., Ranebennur, in MVC no.473/2004, this appeal is filed by claimant seeking enhancement of compensation.
2. Brief facts as stated are that on 26.07.2003, when claimant was traveling in KSRTC bus, it dashed against another KRSTC bus and caused accident.
In accident, claimant sustained grievous injuries.
Despite taking treatment he did not recover fully and sustained permanent physical disability.

Claiming compensation for same, he filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act,
1988, against KSRTC.
3. On service of notice, KSRTC filed objections denying negligence and opposed claim petition on quantum of compensation.
4. Based on pleading, tribunal framed issues and thereafter recorded evidence.
Claimant was examined as P.W.1 and Dr.Kantesh Shankrappa Bhimakkanannvar was examined as P.W.2.
Exs. P.1
to 7 were got marked.

On behalf of respondent driver was examined as R.W.1.
5.

On consideration, tribunal held that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of KSRTC bus by its driver and claimant was entitled for compensation of Rs.1,13,200/- from KSRTC with interest at rate of 6% per annum.
Not satisfied with quantum of compensation claimant is in appeal.
KSRTC has not preferred appeal.
6. B.M.Patil, learned counsel for claimant/appellant submitted that claimant sustained fracture of both bones of right forearm at upper 1/3rd and middle 1/3rd respectively.
P.W.2- doctor who examined claimant for assessment of disability noted mal- union and restriction of movements of hand and loss of grip.
Though P.W.2 assessed limb disability at 45%, tribunal considered 'loss of earning capacity' at meager an extent of 10% and awarded inadequate of compensation.
It was submitted that even award under other heads was grossly inadequate and sought enhancement.
7. On other hand, Sri.M.K.Soudhagar, learned counsel for respondent/KSRTC sought to support award and opposed enhancement of compensation.

It was submitted on overall consideration compensation awarded was just and proper and no enhancement was called for.
8.
Heard learned counsel for both parties, perused impugned judgment and records.

9. From above submission, since KSRTC has not preferred appeal and only claimant is in appeal,
point that would arises for consideration is:
Sri. Nagaraj vs Divisional Manager on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71181594/
2 "Whether claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought?"
10.

sentences.text: Insofar as monthly income, though claimant stated that he was 25 years of age, working as mason and earning Rs.7,000/- per month, same was not substantiated with evidence.

In absence,
tribunal assessed income notionally.
But notional income for year 2003 is Rs.3,250/- therefore same has to be considered.
11. Though P.W.2 has assessed disability at 45% to right upper limb.
Considering limb disability in light of occupation of claimant, tribunal has considered 'loss of earning capacity' at 10%.
There is moderate restriction of movement noted by P.W.2.
But, tribunal has noted that P.W.2 admitted during cross examination that due to disability sustained it cannot be stated claimant would be unable to work as mason.
Taking same into account, I do not see any good or sufficient reasons to interfere with assessment of 'loss of earning capacity'.

Thus future loss of income would be as follows:
Rs.3,250/- x 10% x 12 x 18 = Rs.70,200/-
12.
Tribunal has awarded sum of Rs.22,000/- towards 'pain and suffering'.
Claimant sustained fracture of both bones of right hand at upper 1/3rd and middle 1/3rd.
Considering same award of Rs.22,000/- towards 'pain and suffering' would be inadequate.
If it is enhanced to Rs.35,000/- ends of justice would be met.
Tribunal has awarded Rs.5,000/- towards 'medical expenses'.
Considering fractures sustained no bills were produce, therefore there is no scope for enhancement.
Tribunal has granted Rs.5,000/- towards 'incidental expenses'.
Duration of inpatient treatment is not stated.
Therefore, award appears justified.
Normally fractures take about three months to heal.

Therefore,
'loss of earning during lay off period' would be Rs.9,750/- (Rs.3,250/- x 3).
Tribunal has awarded sum of Rs.15,000/- towards 'loss of amenities', considering disability sustained it would be appropriate to enhance it to Rs.25,000/-..
Thus total compensation would be as follows:

Point for consideration is answered partly in affirmative.
Consequently, I pass following:
